DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorDiagnosis` is declared as a plain class, but the implementation uses dataclass-only field declarations (`evidence: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)`) and instantiates it throughout the immune layer with keyword arguments as if an auto-generated `__init__` exists. Evidence in the provided snippet: unlike `FailureRecord`, `ModelResponse`, and `CorrelatedFailureModel`, `DetectorDiagnosis` is missing the `@dataclass` decorator. A plain class with annotated attributes and `field(...)` has no generated constructor, so every call such as `DetectorDiagnosis(detector="kappa", pathology=..., ...)` in `record_round()`, `record_model_round()`, `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`, `self_diagnose()`, and `check_dispatch_health()` will raise `TypeError: DetectorDiagnosis() takes no arguments`. This is a boundary-critical runtime break for the immune subsystem.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX:
<<<<
class DetectorDiagnosis:
    """Diagnosis from the detector health monitor."""
    detector: str  # "kappa", "mu", "d_decay"
    pathology: str  # human-readable description
    severity: str  # "WARNING", "CRITICAL"
    recommended_action: str  # what to do about it
    evidence: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # IM_F013: Machine-readable key for remediation routing, decoupled from
    # human-readable pathology string. Must match _REMEDIATION_CHAINS keys.
    pathology_key: str = ""
>>>>
====
@dataclass
class DetectorDiagnosis:
    """Diagnosis from the detector health monitor."""
    detector: str  # "kappa", "mu", "d_decay"
    pathology: str  # human-readable description
    severity: str  # "INFO", "WARNING", "CRITICAL"
    recommended_action: str  # what to do about it
    evidence: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # IM_F013: Machine-readable key for remediation routing, decoupled from
    # human-readable pathology string. Must match _REMEDIATION_CHAINS keys.
    pathology_key: str = ""
>>>>
FOLLOW: This fix unblocks every immune emission site that constructs `DetectorDiagnosis`: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()`, `record_model_round()`, `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`, `self_diagnose()`, and `check_dispatch_health()`. It also makes `false_positive_rate`, `all_diagnoses`, and `has_critical` operate on actual structured diagnosis instances instead of failing before population. No further code changes are required in the shown boundary once the decorator is added.
VERIFIED: TRUE

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorHealthMonitor._extended_p_pass_remediation()` computes `Module 4: Detection parameter coherence` unconditionally, even when evaluating ordinary multi-model remediations unrelated to self-adjustment. Evidence: the method always appends a failure if `self._stuck_window >= self._original_stuck_window * 2`, regardless of `chain_key`, `transform_name`, `target_metric`, or whether the proposed transform changes any detection parameter. That means a saturated detector window can cause unrelated remediations like `add_synthesis_directive` to accrue a bogus modular failure and potentially be rejected or downgraded. This is a cross-responsibility bug: self-diagnosis state leaks into unrelated remediation approval.

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorHealthMonitor.self_diagnose()` claims to “iterate toward simplest sufficient” but orders candidates from more complex to less complex. Evidence in Self-check 1: when both windows can change, `candidates` is populated as `("stuck_only", ...)`, `("mu_only", ...)`, then `("both", ...)`. The code comment immediately above says “try adjusting both, then only one, then neither,” which itself contradicts the subsequent “SD-3 fix: try single-parameter adjustments before combined.” More importantly, the execution order shown is single-parameter first, which is simpler; the stale comment is wrong and misstates the safety property. This is not cosmetic only: reviewers or future maintainers can reverse the order to match the misleading comment and reintroduce over-adjustment.
